t: After Sweden left the Kalmar Union in 1523, Denmark and Norway stayed under one Oldenburg king for nearly three centuries.
A Lutheran state funded by the Sound Toll, it became an absolute monarchy in 1660 under the written King’s Law of 1665.
It lost Scania to Sweden in 1658, and defeat as Napoleon’s ally forced it to cede Norway to Sweden in 1814.
dyk: In 1792 Denmark-Norway became the first European state to ban the transatlantic slave trade by law, though the ban only took effect in 1803.
ev: Sweden leaves the Kalmar Union; Frederick I becomes king
Christian III introduces the Lutheran Reformation
Treaty of Knäred ends the Kalmar War in Denmark-Norway’s favour
Treaty of Roskilde cedes Scania and other provinces to Sweden
Frederick III establishes hereditary absolute monarchy
Hans Egede begins the Danish recolonisation of Greenland
Britain bombards Copenhagen and seizes the Danish fleet
Treaty of Kiel cedes Norway to Sweden

f.successor: Kingdom of Denmark; Kingdom of Norway (1814); Sweden-Norway
